Page 1696 
Tezspire (tezepelumab-ekko) 
 
  
  
Prior Authorization Guideline 
 
  
Guideline ID 
GL-713343  
Guideline Name 
Tezspire (tezepelumab-ekko)  
Formulary 
• 
Medicaid - Community & State Arizona  
 
 
Guideline Note: 
Effective Date: 
10/1/2026  
 
 
 
 
1 .  Criteria 
 
Product Name:Tezspire auto-inj  
Diagnosis 
Asthma  
Approval Length 
6 month(s)  
Therapy Stage 
Initial Authorization  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Submission of medical records (e.g., chart notes, lab work, imaging) documenting 
diagnosis of severe asthma  


--- PDF page 1697 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 1697 
 
AND 
 
2 - Patient is 12 years of age or older  
 
AND 
 
3 - ONE of the following:  
 
 3.1 Patient has had two or more asthma exacerbations requiring systemic corticosteroids 
(e.g., prednisone) within the past 12 months  
 
OR 
 
 3.2 Prior asthma-related hospitalization within the past 12 months  
 
AND 
 
4 - Patient is currently being treated with ONE of the following unless there is a 
contraindication or intolerance to these medications:  
 
 4.1 BOTH of the following:  
• 
High-dose inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) (i.e., greater than 500 mcg fluticasone 
propionate equivalent/day)  
• 
Additional asthma controller medication (e.g., leukotriene receptor antagonist [e.g., 
montelukast], long-acting beta-2 agonist [LABA] [e.g., salmeterol], tiotropium)  
 
OR 
 
 4.2 One maximally-dosed combination ICS/LABA product (e.g., Advair [fluticasone 
propionate/salmeterol], Symbicort [budesonide/formoterol], Breo Ellipta [fluticasone/vilanterol]) 
 
AND 
 
5 - Paid claims or submission of documentation (e.g., chart notes) demonstrating history of 
failure, contraindication, or intolerance to ALL of the following:  


--- PDF page 1698 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 1698 
• 
Dupixent (dupilumab)  
• 
Fasenra (benralizumab)  
• 
Xolair (omalizumab)  
 
AND 
 
6 - Prescribed by or in consultation with ONE of the following:  
• 
Pulmonologist  
• 
Allergist/Immunologist  
 
Product Name:Tezspire auto-inj  
Diagnosis 
Asthma  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Therapy Stage 
Reauthorization  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Submission of medical records (e.g., chart notes, lab work, imaging) documenting positive 
clinical response to therapy as evidenced by ONE of the following:  
• 
A reduction in asthma exacerbations  
• 
Improvement in forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) from baseline  
 
AND 
 
2 - Patient continues to be treated with an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) (e.g., fluticasone, 
budesonide) with or without additional asthma controller medication (e.g., leukotriene receptor 
antagonist [e.g., montelukast], long-acting beta-2 agonist [LABA] [e.g., salmeterol], tiotropium) 
unless there is a contraindication or intolerance to these medications  
 
AND 


--- PDF page 1699 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 1699 
 
3 - Paid claims or submission of documentation (e.g., chart notes) demonstrating history of 
failure, contraindication, or intolerance to ALL of the following:  
• 
Dupixent (dupilumab)  
• 
Fasenra (benralizumab)  
• 
Xolair (omalizumab)  
 
AND 
 
4 - Prescribed by or in consultation with ONE of the following:  
• 
Pulmonologist  
• 
Allergist/Immunologist  
 
Product Name:Tezspire auto-inj  
Diagnosis 
Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP)  
Approval Length 
6 month(s)  
Therapy Stage 
Initial Authorization  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Patient is 12 years of age or older  
 
AND 
 
2 - Submission of documentation (e.g., chart notes) confirming ALL of the following:  
 
 2.1 Diagnosis of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis (CRSwNP) defined by ALL of the 
following:  
 
  2.1.1 TWO or more of the following symptoms for greater than or equal to 12 weeks 
duration:  
• 
Mucopurulent discharge  
• 
Nasal obstruction and congestion  
• 
Decreased or absent sense of smell  


--- PDF page 1700 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 1700 
• 
Facial pressure or pain  
 
AND 
 
  2.1.2 ONE of the following:  
• 
Evidence of inflammation on paranasal sinus examination or computed tomography 
(CT)  
• 
Evidence of purulence coming from paranasal sinuses or ostiomeatal complex  
 
AND 
 
  2.1.3 The presence of nasal polyps  
 
AND 
 
 2.2 ONE of the following:  
• 
Patient has required prior sino-nasal surgery  
• 
Patient has required systemic corticosteroids in the previous 2 years  
 
AND 
 
 2.3 Patient has been unable to obtain symptom relief after trial of ALL of the following 
agents/classes of agents:  
• 
Nasal saline irrigations  
• 
Intranasal corticosteroids (e.g., fluticasone, mometasone, triamcinolone)  
• 
Antileukotriene agents (e.g., montelukast, zafirlukast, zileuton)  
 
AND 
 
3 - Paid claims or submission of documentation (e.g., chart notes) demonstrating history of 
failure, contraindication, or intolerance to BOTH of the following:  
• 
Dupixent (dupilumab)  
• 
Xolair (omalizumab)  


--- PDF page 1701 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 1701 
 
AND 
 
4 - Used in combination with another agent for CRSwNP (i.e., intranasal corticosteroids, nasal 
saline)  
 
AND 
 
5 - Patient is NOT receiving Tezspire in combination with another biologic medication [e.g., 
Nucala (mepolizumab), (Xolair (omalizumab), Dupixent (dupilumab)]  
 
AND 
 
6 - Prescribed by or in consultation with ONE of the following:  
• 
Otolaryngologist  
• 
Allergist  
• 
Pulmonologist

failure, contraindication, or intolerance to BOTH of the following:

• 
Dupixent (dupilumab)  
• 
Xolair (omalizumab)  
 
AND

AND 
 
4 - Patient is NOT receiving Tezspire in combination with another biologic medication [e.g., 
Nucala (mepolizumab), (Xolair (omalizumab), Dupixent (dupilumab)]
